chats.answer:
Several portable power stations can be linked together to increase their total power output, but there's an important distinction:

Parallel operation: Combines multiple power stations to increase wattage (W), allowing you to run larger appliances.

Battery expansion: Adds battery capacity (Wh or kWh), increasing runtime but not necessarily output wattage.

If you want to run high-power appliances, such as multiple air conditioners, power tools, or whole-home loads, you need models that support combined AC output, not just extra batteries.

chats.answer:
Several portable power stations can be linked together to increase their total AC output power (watts), but many others only support adding batteries to increase runtime (watt-hours).

The distinction matters:

Parallel operation: Two power stations combine their output to run higher-wattage appliances.

Battery expansion: Extra batteries increase runtime but don't necessarily increase maximum output.

Split-phase operation: Two compatible power stations provide 120V/240V output, useful for larger appliances and home backup.

If you want to run something that requires 5,000W using two 3,000W power stations, you need a system that explicitly supports combining AC output—not just battery expansion.
